doc.title: TEST-terminal-chutes-high
sources: synthetic: geometry chosen to exercise the terminal-chutes topology on the scripted pin table; NOT a read of any table
the wpa TEST fixture (entry height law, support, resistance class) — copied
doc.notes: Serves pockets 1 and 4 (the middles) with a short lead and a terminal chute each; the corners are unserved for the same reason as the wpa fixture (legs under the corner cups). Each chute: 300 mm inboard run dropping 60 mm, stop face at s = 280 mm (capacity floor(280 / 57.15) = 4), a 26 mm up-turn beyond the stop = the stop body (exempt from drain, ≤ one ball diameter).

axes.+Z: left to right viewed from head rail

datum_frame.runtime_mapping: three.js (x, y, z) = (X, Y, Z) x 0.001; kernel (kx, ky, kz) = (Z, X, Y) x 0.001
datum_frame.pocket_order: kernel order: 0 lb, 1 lc, 2 lt, 3 rb, 4 rc, 5 rt (l/r = sign of Z, b/c/t = -X / 0 / +X)

provenance.source: WPA Equipment Specifications §16, 2 1/4 in pool ball (crates/pool-core default r 0.028575)

PROXY: the kernel default class (params.rs ClothPreset::default, u_r 0.010 — Waldron stimpmeter roll-out, a first-hand cloth measurement) stands in for the unmeasured steel-wire class. On the twin rail the effective coefficient is (7/5)(r/ρ)·u_r = 1.4 × 1.322 × 0.010 = 0.0185 (track.js resistCoeff); drain margin at the shallowest edge: sin θ 0.0436 vs 0.0185.

research.md R5 / the brief's 'inelastic arrival' and the owner's 「一个接一个堆」: arriving balls share a common velocity with the group they touch, the tray wall is infinite mass. A modelling decision, NOT a measurement — no ball-on-ball impact in a return tray has been captured in this repo; a measured e would enter through this block and a runtime law change (spec §7).
